types.description: TeSys D contactor, 3 main NO poles, 1 NO + 1 NC factory auxiliaries, 24 V DC coil

modelingNotes: Wiring endpoints follow the exact product sheet page 6: A1, A2; 1/L1–2/T1, 3/L2–4/T2, 5/L3–6/T3 (main NO); 13/NO–14 (auxiliary NO); 21/NC–22 (auxiliary NC). Slash markings are retained verbatim. No additional accessory contacts are included.

Coil: 24 V DC standard, 5.4 W inrush and holding at 20 degrees C; built-in bidirectional peak-limiting diode suppressor. No polarity assignment is asserted. Suppressor behavior is documented here and encompassed by the coil function, without a separate circuit mark or net join.

Main circuit: 9 A AC-3 or 25 A AC-1 at up to 440 V AC and ambient at most 60 degrees C. Operational capability up to 690 V AC 25–400 Hz or 300 V DC is not assigned nominal voltage. Contact current and voltage scalar ratings are omitted because limits depend on use category and conditions.

Coil mechanically actuates all five contacts. Neither normally closed state, coil winding nor suppression is permanent wiring; no fixed links. Coil A1 and A2 are required for the operational contactor abstraction; switched contact usage is application-dependent.

All twelve schematic endpoints are represented. Physical duplicated coil access points and their internal links are not established by these schematic documents; coverage remains partial. No PE, shield or communication connection is documented or invented. Add-on blocks and mounting assembly bonding are outside this bare contactor scope.

Schneider FAQ FA121938 (published2007-08-28, modified2026-05-12; https://www.se.com/us/en/faqs/FA121938/) explicitly applies to LC1D***D DC coils and instructs A1 positive, A2 negative. This includes LC1D09BD. The absence of polarity signs on the simplified circuit diagram and bidirectional suppressor wording do not establish non-polar wiring.

connectionCoverage.notes: Complete twelve-endpoint circuit diagram inventory; physical duplication of coil access and any corresponding hardware links remain unverified. Built-in suppression is documented but not separately drawn.
